paragraphs: Friend, look at who is in the room in this passage. Pilate asks, "What evil has He done?" (Mark 15:14), and nobody gives him an answer. The crowd just shouts "all the louder" (Mark 15:14). Pilate knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over (Mark 15:10), and he still gave the crowd what it wanted.

Now look at Jesus. He is questioned, accused of many things, struck, spit on and bowed to in mockery, and He doesn't hit back with a single word of defense. To Pilate's amazement, Jesus made no further reply (Mark 15:5). I think that silence is not weakness. He is not a man being dragged along, and the passage shows Him walking toward the cross, and I'd say that is the whole point of Mark 10:45, where Jesus says that the Son of Man came "to give His life as a ransom for many."

Here's why it matters to you, baker. Barabbas, a man held with rebels who had committed murder (Mark 15:7), walks out free while Jesus is handed over to be crucified (Mark 15:15). I can't tell you what Barabbas did next, because Mark doesn't say. But I know what it's like to sit in a dark place and not deserve a rescue, and to get one anyway. That is the kind of love that keeps my ovens warm, friend, and this story is far from over.
